candidates.name: 日本製鉄 (Nippon Steel)
candidates.rationale: Q1 FY2026 (Apr-Jun 2026, reported 2026-08-04) business profit rose 58.1% YoY to JPY 145.5bn, driven by the acquired U.S. Steel turning profitable. On the back of this, Nippon Steel raised its FY2027/3 full-year guidance: business profit from JPY 530bn to JPY 630bn and net profit from JPY 220bn to JPY 290bn, citing stronger U.S. steel prices and U.S. Steel's improved profitability (U.S. Steel segment full-year business-profit guidance raised to over JPY 180bn). Fills a materials/steel gap in the pool (currently zero coverage) and diversifies away from the pool's heavy bank/trading-house/auto weighting; not itself a heavy oil-cost importer like chemicals/autos, so less exposed to the macro's Hormuz-driven input-cost headwind.

candidates.name: セブン&アイ・ホールディングス (Seven & I Holdings)
candidates.rationale: FY2026/2 (year ending Feb 2026) guidance calls for consolidated net profit up 47% YoY to JPY 255bn. Capital returns are large and credible: a buyback of up to JPY 600bn (up to 400m shares, 15.4% of shares outstanding ex-treasury) ran 2026-04-10 through 2026-02-28, part of a JPY 2 trillion buyback program through FY2030 announced March 2026; the company also structured its 2026 capital tie-up with SoftBank and other partners around a short-term buyback-and-reissue scheme specifically to avoid share-count dilution while keeping the buyback program intact. FY2026 dividend guidance is JPY 60/share. Diversifies the pool into retail beyond the disabled Fast Retailing name.

candidates.name: 東海旅客鉄道 (Central Japan Railway / JR Central)
candidates.rationale: FY2026/3 (year ended March 2026) results: revenue passed JPY 2 trillion for the first time (~JPY 2,006bn); Shinkansen + conventional line transport revenue rose ~11% YoY to ~JPY 1,585bn on inbound tourism and Osaka-Kansai Expo 2025 demand; operating profit ~JPY 830bn and net profit ~JPY 553bn were both record highs. Chuo Shinkansen (maglev) total project cost was raised to JPY 11 trillion with the opening pushed beyond 2034, but management states it can fund this from internal cash flow while maintaining its financial discipline and dividend. Adds a railway name beyond JR East, currently the pool's only rail exposure.

candidates.name: エーザイ (Eisai)
candidates.rationale: Q1 FY2026 (Apr-Jun 2026, TDnet disclosure 2026-07-29) global Leqembi (lecanemab) sales grew 27% YoY to JPY 29.3bn (Japan: JPY 6.1bn), and the Leqembi business reached commercial-basis (ex-R&D) profitability for the first time in a quarter. The FDA approved the subcutaneous maintenance/auto-injector (iCLICK) formulation on 2026-07-13, with U.S. launch planned for late August 2026, removing a key adoption friction point. FY2026/3 guidance: revenue ~JPY 885bn, operating profit ~JPY 70bn. Flagged at a lower score than the other adds because overall operating margin remains thin (~8%) despite the Leqembi growth narrative; adds pharma diversification beyond the pool's existing three names (Takeda, Daiichi Sankyo, Chugai).

candidates.name: 大阪ガス (Osaka Gas / Daigas Group)
candidates.sector: ガス・エネルギー (Gas utility)
candidates.rationale: FY2026/3 (year ended March 2026) results: record net profit up 14% YoY to JPY 152.7bn, driven by growth in U.S. shale-gas production and a domestic fuel-cost "time-lag" margin benefit; revenue -2% to JPY 2,030.3bn, operating profit +9% to JPY 174.8bn. Shareholder returns: annual dividend raised JPY 10 to JPY 130/share, plus a new buyback of up to JPY 80bn approved for FY2027/3. A cleaner balance-sheet utility diversification pick than TEPCO (no Fukushima-related legacy liabilities), filling a utility/energy gap the pool currently has zero coverage of.

candidates.name: 東京センチュリー (Tokyo Century)
candidates.sector: 総合リース・金融サービス (Diversified leasing/financial services)
candidates.rationale: FY2026/3 results (announced 2026-05-11): record profit for the 4th consecutive year — revenue JPY 1,457.7bn (+6.5%), operating profit JPY 148.3bn (+26.7%), net profit JPY 111.3bn (+30.5% YoY). FY2027/3 guidance is net profit JPY 123.0bn (+10.5%), a 5th consecutive record. Dividend was raised twice within the year (FY2026/3 payout increased from a planned JPY 72 to JPY 80), and FY2027/3 is guided to JPY 90 — a 4th consecutive annual increase (payout ratio ~35.8%). Adds a diversified leasing/financial-services name distinct from the pool's megabank and insurer exposure.

notes: Rejected after research: 9501.JP (東京電力/TEPCO) — Kashiwazaki-Kariwa unit 6 restarted commercial operation 2026-04-16/reached full output cycle by Q1 FY2027, giving a ~JPY 47bn quarterly earnings tailwind, but FY2026/3 guidance still shows a consolidated net loss of JPY -641bn driven by Fukushima Daiichi decommissioning/debris-removal costs, and Q1 FY2027 (Apr-Jun 2026) posted a further net loss of JPY -9.7bn; balance sheet still impaired by legacy liabilities, so it does not clear the 'strong balance sheet / durable earnings' bar despite the real operational catalyst. 9202.JP (ANA Holdings) — FY2026/3 results were record highs (net profit JPY 169.0bn, revenue JPY 2,539.2bn) on inbound/leisure demand plus the NCA cargo-carrier consolidation, but ANA's own FY2027/3 guidance points to net profit falling roughly 43% YoY, i.e. deteriorating forward guidance despite strong trailing results, so it was left out this round. 9064.JP (Yamato Holdings) — FY2026/3 operating profit rose 99.2% YoY on B2B pricing normalization, and FY2027/3 guidance calls for a further +48.4% to JPY 42.0bn, but the most recent quarter (Apr-Jun 2026) posted a YoY profit decline due to upfront 'cost optimization' investment spending, muddying near-term momentum; worth revisiting next cycle once a clean quarter confirms the trend.
